# Reference study

This project studies techniques, not brand assets or proprietary compositions.

- Lusion, https://lusion.co/: a single visual stage supports changing content, with transitions treated as part of navigation. Avoid copying its dark studio identity and tunnel imagery.
- Bruno Simon, https://bruno-simon.com/: interaction is the navigation model, not decoration. Avoid copying the toy car world or game map.
- Active Theory, https://activetheory.net/: depth, pacing and technology are bound to a clear creative premise. Avoid copying its AI navigation or case-study assets.
- Lando Norris, https://landonorris.com/: energetic type, WebGL and responsive motion share one performance language. Avoid its racing brand, orange palette and motion signatures.
- OceanX, https://oceanx.org/: photography and spatial media establish scale before explanatory copy. Avoid its ocean footage and institutional visual identity.
- Awwwards Storytelling collection, https://www.awwwards.com/websites/storytelling/: useful as a survey of chapter pacing and interaction variety, not as a source of layouts to reproduce.
- RCK Portfolio, https://www.awwwards.com/sites/rck-portfolio-r/: strong typography and a cursor system create an authored experience. Avoid its ASCII webcam and morphing hero signature.
- Awwwards Typography collection, https://www.awwwards.com/websites/typography/: editorial hierarchy can carry a page without constant animation. Avoid imitating any individual typographic composition.

## Applied system

FORMED SPACE uses a Bodoni-style display face against a compressed grotesk, warm paper, mineral green and oxide red. Desktop layouts use asymmetrical columns and controlled collisions. Mobile compositions remove those collisions, enlarge the reading type and preserve the image subject. Motion is limited to image masks, navigation and page changes.
